lawyerQuestions.question: How can we legally challenge or modify the clause allowing the landlord to terminate the agreement on 15 days' notice while I am bound by an 8-month lock-in period?
lawyerQuestions.whyItMatters: The agreement binds you to an 8-month lock-in period with heavy financial penalties for leaving early, yet gives the landlord the right to terminate at any time on just 15 days' notice without assigning any reason.

findings.spanText: The Licensee agrees that the first eight (8) months of the License Period, that is, from 1st October, 2026 to 31st May, 2027, shall be a lock-in period during which the Licensee shall not terminate this Agreement or vacate the Licensed Premises.

If the Licensee terminates this Agreement or vacates the Licensed Premises for any reason before the expiry of the lock-in period, the Licensee shall be liable to pay to the Licensor the License Fee for the entire unexpired portion of the lock-in period, and the Licensor shall be entitled to recover such amount from the Security Deposit.
The Licensor may terminate this Agreement at any time, including during the lock-in period, by giving the Licensee fifteen (15) days' written notice, without assigning any reason.

lawyerQuestions.question: Can we negotiate a specific timeline for returning the security deposit and add an interest penalty if the refund is delayed beyond that date?
lawyerQuestions.whyItMatters: The document states the security deposit will be refunded within a vague 'reasonable time' and completely lacks a provision specifying what happens if the landlord fails to return it on time.

findings.spanText: The Security Deposit shall be refunded to the Licensee within a reasonable time after the Licensee has handed over vacant and peaceful possession of the Licensed Premises to the Licensor, subject to the deductions permitted under this Clause 5.

lawyerQuestions.question: Is it standard practice for the tenant to bear all major and minor repair costs, including plumbing, electrical, and appliance replacements, and can we limit this responsibility?
lawyerQuestions.whyItMatters: You are taking on all repair costs for plumbing, electrical wiring, water seepage, and fixtures, which is unusual since major structural repairs are typically the landlord's duty in India.

findings.spanText: The Licensee shall, at her own cost, carry out all repairs to the Licensed Premises, whether minor or major, including repairs to plumbing, electrical wiring, water seepage and leakage, and the replacement of any fixture or appliance that ceases to function during the License Period.

lawyerQuestions.question: Can we remove or adjust the automatic deduction of one month's rent for repainting regardless of the property's condition?
lawyerQuestions.whyItMatters: The terms automatically forfeit one month's rent from your deposit for repainting even if you leave the walls spotless.

findings.spanText: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Agreement, a sum equal to one (1) month's License Fee shall in all cases be retained by the Licensor from the Security Deposit towards repainting of the Licensed Premises, irrespective of the condition in which the Licensed Premises are handed back.

lawyerQuestions.question: How can we add a requirement for the landlord to provide advance notice before entering the premises?
lawyerQuestions.whyItMatters: The landlord is currently permitted to enter your home at any reasonable time with or without prior notice, which compromises your privacy.

findings.spanText: The Licensor, and any person authorised by him, shall be entitled to enter upon the Licensed Premises at all reasonable times, with or without prior notice to the Licensee, to inspect the condition of the Licensed Premises or to show the same to prospective licensees or purchasers.

checklist.item: Budget for the monthly license fee of Rs. 32,000, society maintenance charges, special levies, repair funds, and non-occupancy charges.

findings.spanText: The Licensee shall pay to the Licensor a monthly License Fee of Rs. 32,000/- (Rupees Thirty-Two Thousand only) for the use of the Licensed Premises.

checklist.item: Set up a reliable payment mechanism to ensure monthly rent reaches the landlord on or before the 5th day of each calendar month to avoid steep late fees and 24% annual interest.

checklist.item: Inspect the premises thoroughly before moving in to document existing damage, as the landlord has broad discretion to make deductions from your deposit.

checklist.item: Prepare to cover 100% of the stamp duty, registration charges, and incidental expenses for the agreement.

findings.spanText: The entire stamp duty and registration charges payable on this Agreement, and all incidental expenses thereof, shall be borne and paid solely by the Licensee.
